texts.preamble: Da vs Punjeet Jain Etc. on 1 August, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 43119/2016 Date of Institution : 04.05.2009 Date of reserving judgement : 01.08.2018 Date of pronouncement : 01.08.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus A-1) Sh. Puneet Jain S/o Late Sh. lnder Sen Jain M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash 190, Naya Bans. Delhi 110006 R/o C 388, Surya Nagar, Distt. Ghaziabad (U.P.) A-2) Sh. Vinod Kumar Jain S/o Late Sh. Mauji Ram Jain M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash 190, Naya Bans. Delhi 110006 R/o C 388, Surya Nagar, Distt. Ghaziabad (U.P.) A-3) Sh. Subhash Chand S/o Late Sh. Mauji Ram Jain M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash 190, Naya Bans. Delhi 110006 R/o C 388, Surya Nagar, Distt. Ghaziabad (U.P.) A-4) M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash 190, Naya Bans. Cc No. 43119/2016 Page No. 1/15 Da vs Punjeet Jain etc.
texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 30.04.2008 at about 1.45 PM Food Inspector Sanjeev Kumar Gupta purchased a sample of Gutkha (6 x 55 pouches), a food article for analysis from accused No. 1 DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. Puneet Jain Partner M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash, 190, Naya Bans, Delhi 110006 where the said food article was found stored for sale and where Sh. Puneet Jain along with other partners were found conducting the business of said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted of 6 x 55 pouches of Gutkha taken as such in the form of 6 sealed polythene packets having label declaration as is reproduced on notice in Form 6. Sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Mahendra Kumar SDM/LHA (Kotwali). Food inspector divided the sample then & there into three equal parts. Each counter part of the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act & Rules. The vendor's signature were obtained on the LHA Slip and wrapper of the sample counter- parts. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Puneet Jain and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 30.04.2008. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by FI were signed by accused No. 1 Puneet Jain and the other witness Subedar Mishra, Field Assistant. 3. Accused No. 1 Puneet Jain vendor disclosed at the time of sampling that he has purchased the said pouches of Gutkha from M/s S. P. Jagannath & Sons, 2236, Satya Chambers, Raj Guru Road, Chuna Mandi, Pahar Gani, New Delhi. Bill was not given by the supplier. Simultaneously notice under Section 14-A was send to M/s S. P. Jagannath & Sons, 2236, Satya Chambers, Raj Guru Road, Da vs Punjeet Jain Etc. on 1 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54220580/ 2 Chuna Mandi, Pahar Gani, New Delhi 4. One counter-part ot the sample bearing LHA Code Number 42/LHA/21957 was delivered to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found as under. The report of Public Analyst is as follows : "The sample is covered under the Cigarette & other Tobacco products (Prohibition of advertisement & regulation of trade & commerce supply & distribution) bill 2003. The sample does not contain matter as Adulterant." 5. In the report, the public analyst has also reported that the test for presence of Nicotine in the sample is positive this presence of Nicotin is in violation of rule 44.1 of PFA Rules, 1955. The sampled article of food "Gutkha' is thus adulterated because it is contains Nicotine which is injurious to health. The opinion of Public Analyst regarding the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade. and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Bill, 2003 has no relevance in view of clear provisions of PFA Act & Rules and her positive findings about presence of Nicotine. 6. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Puneet Jain was the vendor-cum-partner of accused No. 4 M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash, 190, Naya Bans, Delhi -110006 at the time of taking sample and as such he is in charge of and responsible for day to day conduct of business of the said firm. Accused No. 4 M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash is a partnership firm having three partners i.e. accused No. 1 Puneet Jain, accused No. 2 Vinod Kumar Jain, accused No. 3 Subhash Jain and as such all the three partners are in charge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said firm. Being a firm M/s Mauji Ram Om DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. Prakash is also liable. 7. The vendor disclosed to the food inspector that the sampled article of food "Gutkha" (Bilbagh brand) was purchased by them from M/s S.P. Jagannath & Sons, 2236, Satya Chambers, Raj Guru Road, Chuna Mandi, Pahar Gani, New Delhi however he did not produce any supporting documents like purchase bill / invoice in proof of the same. On investigation by the Food Inspector M/s S.P.Jagannath & Sons informed that they had not sold the sampled articles of food to M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash as they had stopped the business of trading in Gutkha since 2002. As per label declaration on the package of the sampled article of food "Gutkha", M/s Som Products, C-123, Phase 1, Naraina Industrial Area, Delhi -110026 is its manufacturer, M/s Som Products is a partnership firm having two partners i.e. accused No. 5 Sudhir Kumar Bajpai, accused No. 6 Indra Deo Tripatho and both the partners are incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of business of the said firm. Being a firm M/s Som Products is also liable. M/s Som Products also informed to the Food Inspector that they had not sold "Dilbagh Gutkha" to M/s S. P. Jagannath & Sons for last three-four years and therefore the statement of vendor regarding liable. M/s Som Products also informed to the Food Inspector that they had not sold "Dilbagh Gutkha" to M/s S.P. Jagannath & Sons for last three -four years and theretore the statement of vendor regarding M/s S. P. Jagannath & Sons being supplier is not correct. As such, the vendor and other partners of the firm M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash did not disclosed to the Food Inspector the true name, address and other particulars of the Da vs Punjeet Jain Etc. on 1 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54220580/ 3 person from whom they had purchased the sampled articles of food "Gutkha". DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. 8. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 04.05.2009 alleging violation of section 2 (ia) (a) (b) (h) of PFA Act, 1954 and also in violation of Rule 44 (J) of the PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. During the trial, proceedings qua accused No. 5 Sudhir Kumar Bajpai were abated vide order dated 10.10.2013. 9. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned initially and later on other accused were also summoned. The accused no.1 thereafter exercised his option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. As per CFL report, the sample contained Anti-caking agent i.e. Magnesium Carbonate and has contravenes Rule 62 of PFA Rule 1955. Based on the report of the CFL, notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) PFA Act being violation of Rule 62 of PFA Rules, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 10. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh. Sanjiv Gupta, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh. Mahendra Kumar, PW-3 FA Sh. Subedar Mishra. PW-1 and PW-3 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. Mahendra Kumar. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of six polythene packets of "Gutkha" from the vendor for analysis, bearing identical label declaration, converting the sample into three counterparts by putting two sealed pouches together as one counterpart, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C, notice u/s 14 A Ex.PW1/D. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/e on 01.05.2008. The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW1/H, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/G was received, according to which the sample does not contain any extraneous matter as adulterant, however, the analystic result shows that test for nicotine was found positive in violation of Rule 44(j) of PFA Rules, 1955. Thereafter PW-1 FI Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta during investigation sent a letter Ex. PW1/H to accused Puneet Jain and in response of the same received a copy of partnership deed, Sales Tax Registration Certificate, MCD Renewal Receipt and Form D VAT mark X1 to X4. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex.PW1/I to STO, Ward No. 26 and received its reply. PW-1 also sent letter Ex.PW1/J to M/s S. P. Jagan Nath & Sons and received its reply vide Ex.PW1/J1 wherein it was mentioned that the said firm has DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. stopped the supply of Gutkha since, 2002. M/s S. P. Jagan Nath & Sons also gave a reply of the notice u/s 14A vide Ex.PW1/J2 and Ex. PW1/J3 wherein the firm denied the sale of Gutkha to Da vs Punjeet Jain Etc. on 1 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54220580/ 4 accused M/s Mauji Ram Om Prakash. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex.PW1/K to STO, Ward No. 4 for seeking information on the constitution of M/s S.P. Jagan Nath & Sons and received its reply stating that the registration of the firm was canceled in the year 2005. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex.PW1/L to M/s Som Products. PW-1 also received reply Ex. PW1/M along with photocopy of Partnership Deed and MCD Renewal Receipt mark Y-Y1. After completion of investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent. The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/N. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/O was filed before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/P alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/Q. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 11.Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence. 12. In their defence, the accused examined Sh S.N. Mehindru as DW-1. Thereafter defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 15. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. 16. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under:- (a) The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason. The CFL report has been assailed by the defence on the ground that the sample was analysed by CFL after the expiry of the product in question and the defence has relied upon of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P. Ltd & Ors 1999 (2) FAC399 to sample in question was packed on April 2008 and was best before six months from the date of packing. In the words of Hon'ble Court :- DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. "Sub-section (1) of Section 30 which appears to be relevant only prescribes in effect that ignorance would be of no defence but that does not mean that if there are contraventions of other mandatory provisions of the Act, the Da vs Punjeet Jain Etc. on 1 August, 2018 In The State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd., JT (1996) 10 SC 480 this Court in somewhat similar circumstances said that the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Act deprived the accused to have sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory and adduce evidence of the report so given in his defence. In this connection reference be made to decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal DA vs Punjeet Jain etc. & Ors., [1998] 5 SCC 343 under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram, AIR (1967) SC 970; Chetumal v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr., [1981] 3 SCC 72 and Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf & Anr., [1999] 2 SCC 400 all under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Therefore, placing reliance upon the aforesaid judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in State of Haryana vs Unique Farmaid P. Ltd & Ors, Hindustan Liver Ltd Vs State of Punjab 2011 (1) FAC 192, a benefit of doubt is given to the accused regarding the adulteration of the sample, which is the subject matter of the present case. Reliance is also placed on the judgement Shiv Kumar @Shiwalamal Narumal Chugwani v. State of Maharashtra 2010 (2) FAC 239 and Food Inspector v. Banarsi Das and others 2014(2)FAC 177. 21.
